correctness.rationale: Every bordered constrained word decomposes uniquely using its unbordered shortest border. The three disjoint classes (border 0, border 1, border of length >=2) give exactly the Mahler identity. The polynomial identity yields the scalar Fibonacci convolution. Fibonacci/Binet estimates and \(u_n\le F_{n+2}\) justify the absolutely convergent density series and rigorous tail estimate. Complete direct enumeration at lengths 1..21 and an alternative polynomial decomposition through length 150 agree with the theorem. All n quantified by combinatorial proof, not experimental extrapolation.

value.rationale: Unbordered strings are canonical building blocks for overlap-free synchronization and word matching; imposing the no-consecutive-11 finite-type language is a natural source/channel constraint. The newly derived complete weight spectrum and explicit nonzero limiting density quantify how often such constrained strings are individually border-free. This exact constrained statistic cannot be obtained by a trivial variable substitution from unconstrained fixed-weight tables. The result does not overstate cross-bifix-free code capacity.
